lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 4 (my view): lion passant, date letter 't', George III duty head, maker mark in script reading like GG. Photo 5: lion passant, date letter 'u', duty head, same maker mark. Different date letters so a matched set, not a single-year set. London date letters t and u in this cycle fit 1794/5 and 1795/6. Photo 1: pointed-end Old English pattern with bright-cut borders and a cartouche, engraving worn. Photo 3: clear crack or split at the bowl-stem junction on one spoon.
lots.condition: Worn bright-cut, bowl wear and scratches, one spoon cracked at the bowl junction.
lots.question_for_gowans: Which spoon has the crack at the bowl junction and is it a through-split? Do all five carry the same maker mark, and which date letters appear on the other three?
